categoryName: Home care & cleaning — floor cleaner, toilet cleaner, phenyl, dishwash, scrubbers, brooms, mops, air freshener, insect/mosquito repellent

skuLines.line: Floor cleaner — mass disinfectant surface cleaner, 500ml–1L
skuLines.examples: Lizol Disinfectant Surface & Floor Cleaner (Citrus/Lavender/Floral); Vim Ultrapro Floor Cleaner; Mr. Muscle Floor Cleaner; Domex Floor Cleaner
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; spikes Jul–Sep monsoon (mud tracked in) and Diwali/Baisakhi deep-clean
skuLines.marginBand: 8–14% (MRP-driven MNC line, thin but it anchors the shelf)
skuLines.notes: The trust anchor of the whole category — if Lizol 1L is out of stock, the household assumes ARY is out of floor cleaner entirely. Heavy per rupee of value: 1L of water-based liquid over 30–50 km of hill road. Stock the 1L as the hero, not the 500ml.

skuLines.examples: Lizol 2L & 5L; Mr. Muscle 2L; Gainda Premium Floral 2L; Floorosol Jasmine 5L; Vim Ultrapro 2L
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; institutional pull before term start and after monsoon
skuLines.notes: THE freight-efficient SKU for Baru Sahib: 5L in one HDPE can carries far less packaging and per-litre transport cost than 5×1L. Also the natural buy for Akal Academy hostel/Eternal University housekeeping and the canteens — a township store's volume sits here, not in the 500ml.

skuLines.examples: ITC Nimyle Kids & Pet Safe Herbal Floor Cleaner 4.8L; Patanjali Gonyle; Beco Natural Surface & Floor Cleaner; Koparo Clean Floor Cleaner & Surface Disinfectant
skuLines.marginBand: 18–30% (D2C/eco brands fund higher trade margin than MNC)
skuLines.notes: Directly targeted at married staff quarters with babies and toddlers crawling on the floor — the cohort ARY has and a normal kirana ignores. Patanjali Gonyle at ₹75/L is also the cheapest branded gateway; Nimyle 4.8L is the family-quarters value pack.

skuLines.examples: CamPure Camphor Floor Cleaner 1L; camphor-fragrance regional floor cleaners
skuLines.notes: Culturally the right premium for a Sikh institution — camphor is a familiar, accepted fragrance where a synthetic lavender aerosol is not. Also mildly insect-deterrent, which matters in monsoon. One facing is enough to test.

skuLines.examples: Gainda White Phenyl Disinfectant 1L/5L; SaveMore Pine Phenyl 1L/5L; Trishul Germonil White Disinfectant Phenyl 5L; Doctor Vikrant White Phenyl 2L
skuLines.marginBand: 25–45% — the single best-margin liquid in the category
skuLines.notes: Non-negotiable for institutional cleaning: hostel corridors, dormitory toilets, dining halls, gurdwara washrooms. Gainda 1L at ₹63–75 is the price-point defender against Lizol. Regional phenyl is where the category actually makes money — carry BOTH a national brand and a regional 5L.

skuLines.examples: Gainda Black Phenyl 1L; Trishul Black Phenyl 1L/5L; Cleanzo Black Phenyl 450ml; Doctor Black Phenyl
skuLines.notes: Bought by housekeeping/sweeping staff, not households — drains, outdoor gullies, cattle sheds, back-of-house. Stains and stinks, so it must be shelved away from food and from white phenyl. High-value line for a township with a lot of open drain and yard.

skuLines.examples: Beco Natural refill 2L; Koparo Clean refill 2L; concentrate sachets that make 5L
skuLines.notes: The most hill-logical format in this entire list: a concentrate sachet ships the chemistry and leaves the water behind, cutting freight per wash by 80%+. Worth a deliberate trial at Baru Sahib even though it is still niche in Indian modern trade.

skuLines.examples: MaxKleen 2-in-1 Floor Cleaner & Insect Repellent 500ml/1.25L; Goclean Mosquito Repellent Deodorant Eco Phenyl 5L
skuLines.notes: One-product answer for monsoon ground-floor quarters where crawling insects come in with the damp — sells itself in Aug/Sep and can be de-listed off-season.

skuLines.line: Toilet cleaner — acid liquid, national brand
skuLines.examples: Harpic Disinfectant Liquid Toilet Cleaner (Original / Sparkling Lemon); Harpic Advanced 600ml; Domex; Mr. Muscle Toilet Cleaner; Godrej Spic
skuLines.notes: Harpic is a name-brand purchase — residents ask for 'Harpic', not 'toilet cleaner'. Acid formulation: never shelve above or beside food or dishwash; leak risk on hill road, so keep the carton upright and inspect on receipt.

skuLines.examples: Gainda Disinfectant Liquid Toilet Cleaner 1L; Kleenest Advanced; Sani Fresh Ultra Shine; KlenShine; private-label toilet cleaner
skuLines.notes: The hostel/quarters price point at roughly half of Harpic per litre, and it earns 3× the margin. Multipacks (3×520ml) are the right shape for a hostel warden or a canteen buying for many washrooms at once.

skuLines.line: Toilet cistern / rim block & urinal cubes
skuLines.examples: Harpic Flushmatic In-Cistern Block 100g/150g; Harpic Hygienic Rim Block 26g; Harpic Fresh Power 6; Feel Fresh Flush Matic; Feel Fresh Sani Urinal Cubes 200g
skuLines.notes: Light, small, non-spill, high value per kg — the ideal hill-freight SKU in the whole toilet set. Urinal cubes are an institutional line specifically: boys' hostel and university block washrooms, bought by the housekeeping in-charge.

skuLines.examples: Harpic White & Shine Disinfectant Toilet Bleach 500ml/1L; sodium-hypochlorite bleach
skuLines.notes: Hard hill water leaves mineral staining that a normal cleaner will not shift — this is the SKU that answers 'the pan has gone yellow'. Never store or sell next to acid toilet cleaner; mixed by a resident it releases chlorine gas. Worth a shelf-talker in Punjabi.

skuLines.examples: Harpic Ultra 10X Bathroom Stain Remover 500ml/1L; Roff T16 Professional Tile & Ceramic Cleaner 500ml; Cif Cream Multipurpose; GoTile Pro Tile & Grout; Selzer / Klenzmo Tap & Shower Cleaner
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round, with a post-monsoon Oct spike (grout mildew)
skuLines.notes: A distinct need from toilet cleaner and residents do not substitute: this is walls, floor tiles, grout and taps. In Baru Sahib's hard water + high humidity, black grout mildew is the recurring complaint — Roff T16 and grout cleaners are the honest answer.

skuLines.examples: Local/regional bottled toilet acid, 'tezaab'; regional HCl brands
skuLines.notes: Not sold on q-commerce but a genuine general-store staple, and what sweeping staff actually reach for on badly stained institutional pans. Corrosive: needs a segregated low shelf, no food adjacency, and a conscious decision by ARY on whether to sell it at all in a school township — it is the one line here that can injure a child. Check the HP position before stocking.

skuLines.examples: Loose or packed bleaching powder; regional 500g–5kg packs
skuLines.notes: An institutional-hygiene must for a 5,000-person township on hill water: overhead tank and water-source sanitation, drains, post-monsoon disinfection. This is a Trust/estate-department purchase in 25kg, not a household one. Caking in humidity is the shelf-life problem — buy to a monsoon plan, not a year's cover.

skuLines.examples: Kiwi Dranex / Mr. Muscle Dranex 50g sachets & 375g; Harpic Drain Cleaner Powder 8×45g; DKlog
skuLines.notes: Canteen and hostel kitchen sinks in a cold climate clog with congealed ghee/oil — a high-urgency purchase, and the resident cannot drive 40 km for it. Sachet multipacks are light and non-perishable: ideal safety stock.

skuLines.examples: Vim Lemon Dishwash Gel 480/500ml; Exo Anti-Bacterial Ginger+Lemon 500ml; Dettol Lemon Fresh 400ml; SaveMore Lemon Gel 500ml
skuLines.notes: The trial and hostel-room size. A university student washing two steel plates buys 500ml, never 2L. Keep a bottle-with-nozzle SKU facing forward.

skuLines.line: Dishwash liquid/gel — large 750ml–3L and refill pouch
skuLines.examples: Vim Lemon 750ml/900ml/2L/3L; Exo Neem+Lime 2L; Dettol Lemon Fresh 1.5L; Beco Natural refill 2L; Koparo refill 2L; Giffy Active Salt 2L
skuLines.notes: Family quarters and the two canteens live on the 2L/3L. Refill pouches are the freight win — a 2L pouch weighs a fraction of the bottle it refills. Stock pouch alongside bottle so the household buys the bottle once and the pouch forever.

skuLines.examples: Vim Lemon Bar 275g; Exo Ginger Bar with Bio-Enzymes; Nip Mahabar; regional bars
skuLines.notes: The highest-unit-count line in this whole category for a hostel population: a student washing their own thali buys a ₹10–30 bar, not a gel. Zero cold-chain, near-infinite shelf life, indestructible in transit — the perfect hill SKU. Never let it go out of stock.

skuLines.examples: Vim Lemon 4×200g; Vim Anti-Smell Pudina 5×190g; Exo Ginger 3×200g / 4×90g; Patanjali Super Dishwash Bar 4×225g
skuLines.notes: Patanjali 4×225g at ₹72 is the cheapest cost-per-gram in the category and fits the institution's own value/swadeshi framing. The multipack is also how you get a family to stop buying one bar at a time — better basket, same trip.

skuLines.examples: Exo Ginger Dishwashing Tub 500g & 2×700g; Exo Yuzu Lemon Tub; Vim Lemon Tub 480g
skuLines.notes: The format canteen and langar washing-up staff prefer — a tub sits by the sink and many hands use it without a bar going soft in standing water. Cheap per gram, spill-proof in transit.

skuLines.examples: Vim Dishwash Powder; Exo Dishwash Powder; regional ash/soda scouring powder
skuLines.notes: Older residents and langar hands who grew up with ash and powder will not switch to gel. Cheap, light, dry — worth one facing. Format known from trade practice rather than the q-commerce pages, which lean gel/bar.

skuLines.examples: Vim Shudhham Metal Cleansing Gel for Pooja Items 100ml; Pitambari Shining Powder; tamarind/imli or besan-based traditional cleaner
skuLines.seasonality: Spikes at Gurpurab, Baisakhi, Diwali and before large langar/samagam
skuLines.notes: Specific to what ARY actually serves and easy to miss: a Sikh institution runs langar on very large steel and sarbloh utensils, and the gurdwara has brass. A real recurring institutional purchase plus a festival household spike, at far better margin than dishwash. Do not treat it as a pooja-aisle afterthought.

skuLines.examples: Scotch-Brite Stainless Steel Scrubber Ball; Exo Steel Scrubber; Gala Steel Scrubber & Utensil Scrubber; Softspun mesh scrubber
skuLines.notes: Impulse, tiny, unbreakable, and one of the best margins on the shelf — belongs at the till, not buried in a cleaning aisle. Burnt-bottom karahi from langar cooking guarantees repeat demand.

skuLines.examples: Scotch-Brite Silver Sparks Scrub Pad (Regular 3pc / Large 3pc); Scotch-Brite Scrub Pad 5pc; Gala Sparkle Magic Green Pad 5pc
skuLines.notes: Pairs with every dishwash bar sold — cross-merchandise them physically. 5pc packs are the hostel/canteen shape.

skuLines.line: Sponge scrub, non-scratch pad & magic eraser
skuLines.examples: Scotch-Brite Sponge Scrub 1pc/3pc; Scotch-Brite Non-Scratch & Antibacterial Pad; Scotch-Brite Power Scrub with Steel Loop; Happi Planet Magic Eraser 4pc
skuLines.notes: Non-scratch is the SKU for non-stick pans and the melamine crockery a school dining hall uses — a steel scrubber destroys both. Magic-eraser sponges are the new premium end (wall marks in hostels: genuinely useful here).

skuLines.examples: Positive Vibes Coconut Fiber Scrub Pad 5pc; natural coir pads; jute/loofah dish scrubbers
skuLines.notes: Plastic-free option that fits an institution with an environmental line; small volume, good margin, no downside to trialling one facing.

skuLines.examples: Ratan Brooms Meghalaya Grass R33 & Mizoram Grass R22; Gala Kingkong Meghalaya Grass; Chand Suraj Strong / Stella / maXell; KlenShine Jhaadu King XXL; Dust Out Grass Broom
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; buy-in spikes at term start and pre-festival cleaning
skuLines.marginBand: 35–55%; unbranded local grass broom higher still
skuLines.notes: Every one of ~1,000+ households and every hostel room needs one, replaced 2–3× a year — a high-unit, high-margin line disguised as a boring one. Bulky and light: freight is charged on volume, so buy in full-carton lots timed to a truck, not weekly. A local Himachal/Meghalaya grass source may beat branded on both cost and margin.

skuLines.examples: Gala No Dust Floor Broom / No Dust XL; Kleeno No Dust Broom by Cello; Scotch-Brite Washable No Dust Classic Broom (+ refill); Dust Out Plastic Floor Broom; Chand Suraj DustBina
skuLines.notes: Washable and lasts far longer than grass, which matters when the nearest replacement is 40 km away — genuinely the better buy for a hill household. Stock the refill head too, or the upgrade story falls apart on second purchase.

skuLines.examples: Gala Chandra Kharata; Chand Suraj Bathroom Broom; regional hard plastic-bristle broom
skuLines.notes: Wet bathroom floors, verandahs and outdoor steps — a soft jhadu is useless on them. Institutional housekeeping buys these by the dozen for hostel washroom blocks.

skuLines.examples: Ratan Brooms Seekh Jhadu (Coconut Fibre); local sinkh/bamboo yard broom
skuLines.notes: Outdoor sweeping: campus paths, courtyards, leaf litter, wet mud. Cheapest broom on the shelf and often the best-margin. A township with a lot of open ground gives steady estate-department demand.

skuLines.examples: Gala V-Ceiling Broom Stick (Nylon); Gala No Dust 2-in-1 with Extendable Long Handle; Tekcool 3-in-1 Long Handle Ceiling Duster
skuLines.notes: High-ceiling hostel dormitories and dining halls make this an institutional tool, not a household nicety. Extendable versions also stop elderly residents climbing on chairs — a real safety sell.

skuLines.examples: Chakaachak Floor Cleaning Pocha; Gala Microfiber Advance Floor Cloth; Proclean Cotton Refill 350g; plain cotton pocha
skuLines.notes: Cheapest entry to wet mopping and the format most households here actually use (hand pocha, not a mop). Wears out fast in monsoon = genuine repeat. Light and compressible: near-zero freight cost per rupee earned.

skuLines.line: Clip / T-mop with telescopic handle + refills
skuLines.examples: Gala T-Mop Cotton Mop; Monkey 555 Premium Clip Mop; Scotch-Brite Cotton Mop with Telescopic Handle; Proclean Clip & Fit Cotton Refill 350g
skuLines.notes: The no-bending upgrade from a hand pocha — the right recommendation for elderly residents and for anyone mopping a whole quarter. Always stock the matching refill: the razor-and-blades economics are the point.

skuLines.line: Spin bucket mop set (360°) + refill discs
skuLines.examples: Chakaachak Eco Spin Bucket Mop; Spotzero by Milton Mini Spin Mop; Esquire Elegant 360 Spin Mop Set; Gala Quick Spin / Aqua Spin; Cello Deluxe Spin Mop Bucket; Gebi Aqua Bucket Spin Mop
skuLines.notes: The genuine premium end and the highest-ticket item in the category — a ₹1,000+ sale to a teaching-staff household ARY currently loses to a town trip. Bulky, so carry 2–3 SKUs and a display piece rather than depth, and hold refill discs so the sale repeats.

skuLines.line: Floor squeegee / wiper with steel handle
skuLines.examples: Proclean Floor EVA Wiper 16" & Big 20"; Chakaachak Shine Floor Wiper 30cm; Scotch-Brite Bathroom Squeegee Wiper (telescopic); Gala Long Handle Tile & Floor Scrubber
skuLines.notes: In a heavy-monsoon hill location this is not optional — it is how you clear water off a bathroom or verandah floor before it goes slippery. Institutional washroom blocks buy multiples.

skuLines.examples: Chakaachak Eazo Wiper & Mini Kitchen Wiper; Gala Ezee Squeegee Sink Wiper; Scotch-Brite Kitchen Wiper; Gebi Bathroom/Window Wiper 82cm
skuLines.notes: Sub-₹100 impulse with excellent margin — Chakaachak Eazo at ₹48–80 sells in volume. Also the window-condensation tool for a cold hill winter, which residents will not have thought to ask for.

skuLines.examples: Gala Double Hockey Toilet Brush with Container; Gala Antibacterial Double Hockey; Scotch-Brite Round Toilet Brush; Venus Brush Industries; RUSH double-sided
skuLines.notes: Bought with the toilet cleaner and replaced roughly yearly. Bulky-but-light so freight is on volume: buy full cartons. Two price points (₹180 workhorse, ₹300 with-container) covers hostel and staff-quarter buyers.

skuLines.line: Tile & bathroom scrubbing brush, long handle
skuLines.examples: Scotch-Brite Tough Bathroom Tile Brush; Scotch-Brite Long Handle Bathroom Tile Scrubber; Gala Hardy Floor Scrubber; Perpetual rotatable bathroom brush
skuLines.notes: Answers the same mildew-grout problem as the tile cleaner — sell the pair. Long handle again removes the bending/kneeling barrier for older residents.

skuLines.examples: Scotch-Brite Multipurpose Microfiber Wipes; Kleeno Multipurpose Microfiber Kitchen Cloth 5pc; Gala Duster (Microfiber); Proclean Microfiber 300gsm; Ratan Simpli Clean Cotton Kitchen Cloth
skuLines.marginBand: 40–60% — one of the best in the category
skuLines.notes: Flat, light, unbreakable, no expiry, high margin: as close to a free-freight SKU as home care has. Multipacks are the right shape for hostels and the canteen. Cotton kitchen cloth at ₹106/6pc is the value defender.

skuLines.examples: Tekcool Extendable Fan Cleaning Duster Set; Tekcool 2-in-1 / Feather Ceiling Duster; Zulaxy Flexible Extendable Duster; Flyngo Microfibre Feather Duster
skuLines.notes: Sharp seasonal peak: fan cleaning before the warm months and before Diwali/Gurpurab. Buy for that window rather than holding year-round stock.

skuLines.examples: Soham Housewares Silicon Gloves; Perpetual Magic Silicone Dish Washing Gloves; plain rubber household gloves
skuLines.notes: Real seasonal logic for Baru Sahib: washing up in near-freezing hill water in December is painful, and gloves are the answer nobody stocks. Also PPE for staff handling phenyl, acid and bleaching powder — arguably a duty-of-care line for the institution.

skuLines.examples: Cello / Nayasa / Milton plastic bucket 13–20L; Prince/Aristo tub; plain mug
skuLines.notes: Nests inside itself, so a stack of buckets ships far better than the volume suggests — the one bulky plastic line worth carrying. Every arriving hostel student needs one, making this a term-start burst rather than a flat line.

skuLines.examples: Kolorr Magnum 14L Pedal / Go Clean 23L; Cello Plastic Pedal; Nayasa Crest & Mikado; Skitch stainless steel pedal & open perforated; Gluman open-top
skuLines.notes: The bulkiest line here — freight is charged on air, so restrict to 3–4 sizes and buy on a full-truck cadence with the buckets. Wet/dry segregation is a live requirement for an institutional campus; a matched pair sells better than singles.

skuLines.examples: Crystal Medium Black Garbage Bag Roll 30pc; Smart One Medium 30pc; Ezee Medium 30pc; Shalimar Medium 4×30pc
skuLines.notes: Highest-repeat consumable in the non-chemical half of the category and it never spoils — the safest line to hold deep stock on before a monsoon road closure. Multi-roll packs are the hostel/canteen shape.

skuLines.examples: Crystal Large 15pc & XL 30×37" 10pc; Ezee Large 24×32"; Shalimar Large 4×15pc & Jumbo XL 42×48"; Happy Shield XL
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; spikes after langar/samagam and festivals
skuLines.notes: Jumbo 42×48" is squarely an institutional SKU: dining-hall, hostel-block and campus-wide waste collection. Large events (samagam, convocation) create a step-change in demand worth planning stock against.

skuLines.examples: Ezee Biodegradable Medium 19×21"; Beco Biofriendly Medium & Large
skuLines.notes: Priced within ₹10–20 of conventional, so the switch costs the household almost nothing — an easy fit for an institution that wants a visible green position on campus waste. Shorter shelf life than plastic (starts to degrade); do not overstock.

skuLines.examples: Colin Glass Cleaner 500ml/1L/3×500ml; Mr. Muscle Glass Cleaner; Maxkleen Multi Shine; Trishul Sparkle Glass Cleaner
skuLines.seasonality: Winter condensation and pre-festival window cleaning
skuLines.notes: Colin is a named-brand ask. Trigger heads crack on a rough hill road and a leaked trigger bottle ruins the carton beneath it — receive these carefully and stock the 1L refill so the household reuses the sprayer.

skuLines.examples: Lizol Kitchen Cleaner & Degreaser 450ml; Mr. Muscle Kitchen Cleaner Spray 450ml; Cif Cream 500ml; BECO Max Kitchen Cleaner; Blueoxy Degreaser
skuLines.notes: Chimney, hob and tile grease — a distinct job from dishwash and residents do not substitute. The two canteens and langar kitchen are the anchor buyers; consider whether an institutional 5L degreaser is worth sourcing for them.

skuLines.examples: Dettol Antiseptic Liquid 250ml/750ml; Dettol Liquid Disinfectant for Floors 1L; Savlon; Lysol Multi-Surface
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; spikes in flu season and any campus outbreak
skuLines.notes: Dual-use (first aid + surfaces) so it doubles as a health-aisle line, and it is the SKU a residential school infirmary and hostel warden want on hand. In a closed township an outbreak makes this a run-on-the-shelf item — hold real buffer stock.

skuLines.examples: Savlon Surface Disinfectant Spray 170g; Lizol/Dettol surface spray; disinfectant surface wipes
skuLines.notes: Aerosol/pressurised cans need cool storage away from heaters and a check against any hostel fire-safety rule before bulk stocking. Wipes are the format for staff-quarter families with babies (high chairs, changing surfaces).

skuLines.examples: All Out Ultra machine + refills; Good Knight Flash / Activ+ machine + refills; Mortein Insta5; Tru Nature paediatrician-certified vaporiser
skuLines.seasonality: Apr–Oct; near-zero Dec–Feb at this altitude
skuLines.notes: Genuinely seasonal here, unlike the plains — Rajgarh's cold winter kills demand for roughly a quarter of the year, so buy Mar–Apr and run down by Nov instead of holding flat stock. Machine-plus-refill combos lock in the refill annuity; the 4× and 6× refill packs are the ones to depth on. Household insecticides fall under the Insecticides Act 1968 — confirm what HP requires for a retail licence before widening this set.

skuLines.examples: Good Knight Maha Jumbo Coil 10pc; Maxo Coil; Tortoise Coil
skuLines.notes: The no-electricity, no-machine option at ₹47/10 — right for hostel rooms and outdoor/verandah use. Open flame in a dormitory is a fire-safety question the school may have a view on; ask before pushing volume.

skuLines.examples: Good Knight Advance Fast Card 10pc; mosquito mats
skuLines.notes: ₹10 price point — the pocket-money purchase for a hostel student with no vaporiser socket. Tiny, flat, weightless: costs nothing to carry.

skuLines.line: Personal mosquito repellent — cream, roll-on, patches
skuLines.examples: Odomos Naturals Non-Sticky Cream 100g; Odomos Lotion 120ml; Good Knight Natural Mild Bloom Fabric Roll-On; Mother Sparsh DEET-free patches
skuLines.notes: Built for exactly the cohorts ARY has and a normal store under-stocks: babies and small children in staff quarters, and school children out on campus at dusk. DEET-free patches and fabric roll-ons are the paediatric-safe formats parents specifically look for.

skuLines.examples: Mortein Advanced Electric Mosquito Racquet; Eveready MR-07 Racquet; Eveready 2-in-1 Racquet & Zapper with UV
skuLines.notes: No chemicals, no smoke, rechargeable — the format a hostel warden can allow where a coil or aerosol is banned. Good margin and a real ticket size; a few pieces with a demo unit is enough.

skuLines.line: Cockroach control — gel bait, chalk, spray
skuLines.examples: HIT Anti Roach Gel 15g; HIT Chalk Cockroach Killer 15g; HIT Crawling Cockroach Killer Spray 400ml/700ml; Baygon Max; Mortein Cockroach Killer; Lakshman Rekha chalk
skuLines.notes: The ₹20 chalk is the mass entry point and the 700ml aerosol the institutional answer for kitchens and dining halls — carry both ends. Aerosols are flammable pressurised goods: cool, segregated storage, and they travel badly in a hot vehicle.

skuLines.examples: Maxo Flying Insect Killer 400ml; Baygon Max Mosquito & Fly Killer 400ml/625ml; Mortein 2-in-1 Insect Killer Spray
skuLines.notes: Flies, not mosquitoes, are the dominant monsoon insect problem around canteens, a fruit-and-veg counter and anywhere with food waste — arguably a bigger real need at Baru Sahib than mosquito control, and a natural cross-sell to the F&V counter's own operations.

skuLines.line: Bed bug, lizard, ant & termite repellent
skuLines.examples: Good Morning Bed Bug Killer Spray 250ml/400ml; Herbal Strategi Ant / Bed Bug / Termite Repellent; Tru Nature & Repl Lizard Repellent Spray; Terminator Eco-Friendly Termite Killer; Gecko Ant Repellent
skuLines.seasonality: Monsoon; bed bugs peak after term start
skuLines.notes: Bed bugs in shared hostel mattresses are a predictable, recurring and embarrassing problem in any residential school — the store that quietly stocks the spray owns that trip. Damp hill masonry also brings termites into wooden furniture and door frames.

skuLines.line: Rodent control — cake, glue board, trap
skuLines.examples: Mortein Rat Kill Cake 100g; rat glue boards; snap traps; regional rodenticide cake
skuLines.seasonality: Onset of cold Oct–Dec (rodents move indoors); grain-storage season
skuLines.notes: Real need for a township with kitchens, godowns and grain storage, and rodents come inside as the hills turn cold. But rodenticide near a school with 5,000 residents including small children is the highest-risk item in this list: glue boards and snap traps are the safer sell, poison cake needs locked storage, sale-to-staff-only discipline, and a check on HP licensing before you carry it.

skuLines.examples: Naphthalene balls; camphor (kapoor) tablets; silica-gel and calcium-chloride damp-absorber packs
skuLines.seasonality: Monsoon Jun–Sep and the damp months either side
skuLines.notes: The most Baru-Sahib-specific line here and the one a plains-designed assortment would miss entirely: heavy monsoon plus cold walls means mildewed almirahs, musty woollens and fungus on leather. Camphor also fits the institution culturally. Dry storage is essential — these absorb moisture on your own shelf if held through a wet season.

skuLines.examples: Odonil Room Freshener Spray 220ml (Citrus/Jasmine); Godrej aer Room Freshener Spray 180ml (Jasmine/Lavender/Rose/Fresh Lush Green)
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; winter peak when windows stay shut
skuLines.notes: Winter demand is higher here than in the plains — closed rooms with no ventilation for months. Avoid the 'after smoke' variants: a tobacco-free Sikh institution is the wrong place for that SKU and stocking it reads badly.

skuLines.line: Air freshener gel pocket, block & zipper pouch
skuLines.examples: Odonil Gel Pocket 10g; Odonil Mix Gel Pocket 3pc; Odonil Nature Zipper Mix 3pc/5pc; Odonil Neem Blocks 4×48g; Godrej aer Power Pocket; BAY6 Bathroom Blocks 4×50g
skuLines.notes: Small, light, no spill, no expiry pressure and multipacks that suit institutional washroom blocks — the best freight-to-value ratio in air care. Multipacks are the SKU for a hostel warden fitting out twenty washrooms at once.

skuLines.line: Electric plug-in / automatic air freshener + refills
skuLines.examples: Godrej aer Plug machine + 2 refills; Godrej aer Matic automatic machine + refill; Air Wick automatic refill 250ml
skuLines.packSizes: machine + 2 refills; 20/25ml plug refills; 210ml, 250ml aerosol refills
skuLines.notes: The premium end of air care and a plausible small gift. Only worth it if you commit to holding the refills — a plug machine sold without a refill supply becomes a complaint, and there is no other shop to buy the refill from.

skuLines.examples: Campure Original Camphor Cone 60g; camphor-based room diffusers
skuLines.notes: Fits this institution unusually well — camphor is already familiar and acceptable in a way a synthetic aerosol is not, and it doubles as a mild insect deterrent. Crosses over to the pooja/gurdwara aisle, so it earns two facings.

skuLines.examples: Loose soda ash / washing soda; citric acid (nimbu sat); descaling powder for kettles and vessels
skuLines.notes: Hard hill water scales kettles, geysers, taps and canteen vessels, and no branded cleaner is as cheap or effective. Very high margin, dry, indestructible in transit. Traditional cleaners the older residents already know how to use.

skuLines.examples: Cherry Blossom Wax Polish & Liquid Shine; Kiwi Shoe Polish; shoe brush; white canvas shoe cleaner
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; heavy at term start and before functions
skuLines.notes: Boundary line — modern trade files shoe care inside home cleaning (Blinkit puts it under Cleaners & Repellents), and for ARY it is unmissable: a residential school of uniformed children means thousands of black leather shoes needing polish, plus white canvas cleaner for PT and sports days. If this sits in another buyer's lane, make sure it is not falling between the two.

trends2026: Eco / plant-based home care has moved from niche to mainstream shelf presence — Beco, Koparo Clean, Happi Planet, Herbal Strategi, Tru Nature, Gecko and Klenzmo all now sit alongside HUL/RB on q-commerce with heavy review volumes (Beco floor cleaner shows 6.3k ratings on Zepto), and they fund 20-30% trade margin against the 8-14% the MNC lines give.

Refill pouches and concentrates are the fastest-moving format change: Beco and Koparo now list 2L refill pouches as separate SKUs, Vim has gone to 3L, and the whole logic is to stop shipping the bottle. For a store 30-50 km up a hill road this is the single most relevant trend in the category.

'Kids-and-pet-safe' and paediatrician-certified positioning has become its own shelf: ITC Nimyle Kids & Pet Safe, Tru Nature paediatrician-certified vaporiser refills, Mother Sparsh DEET-free patches, Gecko baby-safe ant spray. Claim-led premium aimed at exactly the married-staff-with-babies cohort at Baru Sahib.

Q-commerce private labels are taking the value end away from regional brands: Blinkit's SaveMore (phenyl, toilet cleaner, dishwash gel) and Zepto's Chakaachak (pocha, wipers, spin mops) undercut branded equivalents by 40-60% at shelf. The read-across is that a private-label or locally-sourced value tier is now a normal expectation, not a downgrade.

Non-chemical mosquito control is growing against coils and vaporisers: rechargeable racquets/zappers (Mortein, Eveready 2-in-1 with UV), fabric roll-ons and skin patches — suits institutions that restrict open flame and aerosols in dormitories.

The floor-tool upgrade cycle: 360-degree spin bucket mops (₹550-2,500) and telescopic squeegees have largely replaced the bucket-and-pocha in aspirational households, creating a genuine ₹1,000+ ticket in a category that used to top out at ₹200 — plus a refill-disc annuity behind it.

Biodegradable and compostable garbage bags (Ezee Biodegradable, Beco Biofriendly) now price within ₹10-20 of conventional, so the switch is close to free for the household and easy for an institution to mandate campus-wide.

Camphor as a fragrance and air-care platform has crossed from ritual use into mainstream home care — CamPure Camphor Floor Cleaner and Campure Camphor Cones both list with strong ratings. Culturally a much better fit for a Sikh institution than synthetic 'after smoke' aerosols.

SKU proliferation inside the bathroom: toilet cleaner, bathroom/tile stain remover, grout cleaner (Roff T16, GoTile Pro) and tap/shower cleaner (Selzer, Klenzmo, A-Zi) are now four separate purchases where there used to be one. In hard water plus high humidity these are real distinct needs, not marketing.

Multi-function 2-in-1s are being pushed hard as a way to hold shelf in small stores — MaxKleen 2-in-1 Floor Cleaner & Insect Repellent, Mortein 2-in-1 mosquito + cockroach, Goclean Mosquito Repellent Eco Phenyl.
adjacentServices: Institutional supply contract with The Kalgidhar Trust estate/housekeeping department — 5L phenyl, 25kg bleaching powder, jumbo garbage bags, brooms and toilet brushes by the dozen on a standing monthly indent rather than counter sale. In a 5,000-resident township this is where the category's volume actually is.

Monsoon and term-start 'cleaning kit' bundles — a fixed-price hostel kit (bucket, mug, dishwash bar, scrubber, pocha, broom, phenyl, garbage bags) for arriving students, and a staff-quarters monsoon kit (squeegee, hard broom, naphthalene/damp absorber, floor cleaner, insect spray). Removes the guesswork for a first-time buyer and lifts basket size on the highest-traffic weeks of the year.

Refill-and-return station for floor cleaner, phenyl and dishwash liquid — resident brings the bottle, ARY dispenses from a 20-50L institutional can. Cuts freight per litre, cuts plastic on campus, and captures the margin that currently leaks to packaging.

Paid campus pest-control rounds (cockroach gel baiting in canteens and hostel kitchens, monsoon fly control around the F&V counter, rodent boards in godowns) — a service the estate department is likely buying from outside today, sold with the product it consumes.

Equipment repair and spares counter — mop refill discs, broom refill heads, squeegee blades, vaporiser machines. A ₹1,000 spin mop with no replaceable disc within 40 km is a dead purchase; stocking the spare is what makes the premium tool sellable at all.

Sharp counter advice on what NOT to mix — acid toilet cleaner with bleach, phenyl on the wrong surface, rodenticide storage. In a closed township with small children this is both a safety duty and the thing that makes the store trusted rather than merely convenient.

METHOD AND HONESTY NOTE: brands, pack sizes and prices above were pulled LIVE on 2026-08-28 from Blinkit and Zepto. Prices are q-commerce selling prices with the struck-through figure approximating MRP, so treat the UPPER end of each priceBand as the MRP-ish retail level ARY would actually sell at. Margin bands, frequency, cohort and seasonality are Indian FMCG trade-practice ESTIMATES plus reasoning about the Baru Sahib population — they were NOT scraped, and should be confirmed against ARY's own purchase and sales data before anyone plans buying against them.

BLOCKED / NOT REACHED — so this assortment leans on Blinkit + Zepto rather than the full modern-trade set: bigbasket.com returned Akamai 403 to both plain fetch and headless browser; jiomart.com, dmart.in, amazon.in, hul.co.in/brands/home-care and godrejcp.com all 403'd or served empty JS shells; grandviewresearch and mordorintelligence sit behind Cloudflare. The session's WebSearch budget (200/200) was already exhausted before this task began and Bing / DuckDuckGo / Brave all served bot challenges, so NO 2025-26 market-report or trend article was read — the trends2026 list is inferred from the live catalogue evidence itself (which brands, formats, claims and pack sizes are actually on shelf, with what review volumes), not from published trend coverage. Confidence: high on brands/packs/prices (directly observed), medium on the trend list (inferred from shelf evidence), low-to-medium on margin bands (trade knowledge, unverified).

NOT ON Q-COMMERCE, included from Indian general-store trade knowledge and flagged as such in their notes: bleaching powder, hydrochloric toilet acid, washing soda, citric acid, utensil scouring powder, naphthalene balls (the Zepto query for these returned insecticides instead), and shoe polish.
